title: What will happen
description: Say what you are going to do, and what will happen.

explanation.summary: Spanish has two ways to talk about the future. The common one is ir a + an infinitive, which is what people actually use when they are making plans. The other is the simple future, a single verb ending in -é, which is used for predictions and for things that will happen on their own.

sections.heading: Plans: ir a + infinitive
sections.body: For what you intend to do, Spanish uses ir a followed by an infinitive: voy a estudiar, vas a venir. It is the normal way to talk about plans, and it is often shorter than the simple future. You can also use the simple future with ir: voy a ir al médico, and the two together are not wrong, just more emphatic.

examples.en: I am going to study Spanish.
Are you going to come to the party?

sections.heading: Predictions: the simple future
sections.body: The simple future is one verb: hablo, hablaré, hablarás, hablará, hablaremos, hablaréis, hablarán. For -ir verbs it drops the r of the infinitive: comer becomes comeré. For -er and -ar verbs the ending is added to the whole infinitive: hablar becomes hablaré. It is used for predictions and for things that happen by themselves: mañana lloverá, el tren llegará tarde.

examples.en: It does not matter, I will talk to you tomorrow.

sections.heading: Two ways, one meaning
sections.body: Voy a ir al médico and iré al médico say the same thing. The first sounds closer to what you have decided. The second sounds more like a fact about the future.
